bingo.resultBad: The head of procurement wrote something in the margin. It didn't look good.

meeting.title: Pitch meeting
meeting.intro: Three people from {{customer}} are waiting with coffee and a checklist. Answer three questions.
meeting.brief: What you know about the customer:
meeting.question: Question {{n}} of 3

learned.concrete: The panel liked concrete answers best. Worth remembering.
learned.visionary: The panel liked the big vision best. Worth remembering.
learned.humble: The panel liked honesty and humility best. Worth remembering.
learned.buzzword: The panel liked the buzzwords best. No judgement.

reactions.love: The panel nods eagerly. Someone writes "good!" in the margin.
reactions.hate: The head of procurement makes a note. It doesn't look positive.

continuity.q: How do you ensure continuity in the team?

a.concrete: Every role has overlap and we have a documented handover routine.
a.visionary: We build a team that lives on long after we're gone.
a.humble: We know it's a risk, and we're open about how we handle it.
a.buzzword: Through a holistic, cross-functional competence strategy.

public_sector.q: What public sector experience do you have?

a.concrete: We've delivered three similar solutions in the last two years. Here are the references.
a.visionary: We want to help shape the public services of the future.
a.humble: Less than some competitors, but we learn fast and listen well.
a.buzzword: We have a clear digital transformation strategy for the public sector.

a.concrete: Yes, two people on Monday and the rest within two weeks.
a.visionary: We've already started – in our heads.
a.humble: We'll do our best, but we won't promise more than we can keep.
a.buzzword: We have an agile onboarding value stream that scales.

changes.q: What do you do when requirements change along the way?

a.concrete: We bring it into the next sprint planning and show the budget impact.
a.visionary: Change is the whole point. That's where real innovation happens.
a.humble: We talk to you about it early, before it becomes a problem.
a.buzzword: We're change-driven, continuous and end-to-end oriented.

a.concrete: Because we've done exactly this before, and we're cheaper than you think.
a.visionary: Because we see what you don't see yet.
a.humble: That's for you to judge, but we think we're a good fit.
a.buzzword: Because we deliver synergy across the whole value chain.

price.q: Your hourly rate is high. Why?

a.concrete: We use fewer hours. Here's the maths.
a.visionary: Quality has its price, but also its value.
a.humble: We can look at it. We'd rather have a good partnership than a high price.
a.buzzword: It reflects our value-based delivery model.

a.concrete: Threat modelling every sprint and automated vulnerability scanning in the pipeline.
a.visionary: Security isn't a requirement for us, it's a culture.
a.humble: We're not experts in everything, but we know when to bring in help.
a.buzzword: Zero trust, DevSecOps and full observability.

a.concrete: The same people on the CVs. Here they are.
a.visionary: A team that's passionate about making a difference.
a.humble: People who are skilled and nice. You can meet them first.
a.buzzword: A self-organising, cross-functional product team.

legacy.q: What do you think of our old system?

a.concrete: We've looked at the code. We suggest replacing one module at a time.
a.visionary: It's the foundation for something completely new.
a.humble: It has served you well for 20 years. We should respect that.
a.buzzword: It's ripe for a cloud-native microservices migration.

a.concrete: We use it where it saves time, and we measure the effect.
a.visionary: AI will change everything. We want to lead the way.
a.humble: We're curious, but careful not to over-promise.
a.buzzword: GenAI-driven innovation with a sustainable data strategy.

dlv_waterfall.q: We're used to waterfall. Do we have to go agile now?

a.concrete: No. We can deliver in phases with fixed milestones and demo something every month.
a.visionary: Method is secondary. What matters is where we're headed.
a.humble: Not at all. We'll adapt to how you work, not the other way round.
a.buzzword: We offer a hybrid, scalable agile-waterfall framework with built-in flexibility.

dlv_deadline_slip.q: What do you do when it's clear the deadline won't hold?

a.concrete: We tell you straight away and offer three options: cut scope, move the date or add people.
a.visionary: Then we lift our gaze and ask what truly has to be there on the day.
a.humble: We say so early, even when it's awkward. You should never be surprised.
a.buzzword: We re-prioritise the backlog end-to-end and re-baseline the delivery.

a.concrete: Automated tests on every change, and a round with real users before each release.
a.visionary: Quality isn't a phase. It's a culture.
a.humble: Thoroughly, but we don't catch everything. That's why we'd like your testers involved.
a.buzzword: We shift left with continuous, fully automated quality assurance across the pipeline.

dlv_code_review.q: Who checks the code before it goes live?

a.concrete: At least one other developer approves every change. Nobody approves their own code.
a.visionary: The whole team. We own the code together – today and ten years from now.
a.humble: A colleague, always. We make mistakes, and better we find them than you.
a.buzzword: We run a cross-functional peer review flow with four-eyes by default.

dlv_documentation.q: Will there be documentation, or just code?

a.concrete: An architecture overview, a runbook and an up-to-date README. It's in the delivery plan.
a.visionary: We document not just what we did, but why – for those who come after.
a.humble: Honestly, docs are rarely perfect. But you'll be able to understand them.
a.buzzword: We deliver living, docs-as-code knowledge management.

dlv_handover.q: What happens when the contract ends?

a.concrete: Four weeks of overlap and a checklist we work through together, item by item.
a.visionary: Then your next chapter begins – on foundations that hold.
a.humble: Then you should manage without us. That's really the goal.
a.buzzword: We ensure a seamless exit transition with end-to-end knowledge transfer.

dlv_status_reports.q: How often do we get status reports?

a.concrete: Every Friday: one page with progress, risks and what we need from you.
a.visionary: You won't need reports. You'll feel the progress.
a.humble: As often as you like. Tell us what's useful and we'll do that.
a.buzzword: We offer real-time dashboards with KPIs and insights across the portfolio.

dlv_meetings.q: Is this going to mean lots of meetings?

a.concrete: A fifteen-minute standup daily and a demo every other week. The rest goes on chat.
a.visionary: We meet when it creates something. Otherwise we let the work speak.
a.humble: We try to keep it down, but tell us if we're taking too much of your time.
a.buzzword: We run a lean ceremony structure optimised for asynchronous alignment.

a.concrete: We keep a risk log with an owner and an action per item, and review it weekly.
a.visionary: The biggest risk is not daring at all. We dare – with our eyes open.
a.humble: We won't spot everything up front, but we'll tell you as soon as we see something.
a.buzzword: Through proactive, holistic risk mitigation embedded in the value chain.

dlv_other_vendors.q: You'll have to work with two other vendors. Is that okay?

a.concrete: Yes. We suggest a shared board, a weekly sync and clear interfaces.
a.visionary: Together we become an ecosystem greater than the sum of its parts.
a.humble: That's fine. We don't have every answer, and others know things we don't.
a.buzzword: We orchestrate multi-vendor synergies in a shared delivery ecosystem.

dlv_mvp.q: What's the smallest thing we could launch?

a.concrete: Login, the application form and a receipt. Everything else can wait for round two.
a.visionary: A small seed that holds the whole tree.
a.humble: You know that best. We'd suggest asking a few of your users first.
a.buzzword: An MVP with minimal friction and maximum value delivery.

dlv_prioritisation.q: Everything is equally important to us. So how do you prioritise?

a.concrete: We rank everything in one list with you. Whatever's on top gets built first.
a.visionary: We ask what you want to be known for in five years, and start there.
a.humble: We can suggest, but you're the ones who know what matters most.
a.buzzword: We use a value-based, data-driven prioritisation matrix with impact scoring.

dlv_success_metrics.q: How will we know the project was a success?

a.concrete: We agree on three metrics today and measure them before and after launch.
a.visionary: When nobody remembers what it was like before.
a.humble: When your users are happy. We'd rather ask them than guess.
a.buzzword: Through a holistic benefits realisation framework with OKRs and KPIs.

dlv_user_involvement.q: Will our users really be involved, or is that just talk?

a.concrete: We test with five users every third week. You get the recordings and findings.
a.visionary: Users won't be involved. They'll be co-creators.
a.humble: That depends on getting access to them. We'll need your help there.
a.buzzword: We run continuous user insight in a human-centred design sprint loop.

dlv_go_live.q: What does launch day look like?

a.concrete: We switch on for ten percent first, watch the errors and roll out the rest the next day.
a.visionary: Like the start of something, not the end.
a.humble: Hopefully boring. And if it isn't, we'll all be there.
a.buzzword: A phased, risk-minimised canary rollout with full observability.

dlv_on_call.q: Who picks up if the system goes down at 3 a.m.?

a.concrete: We run an on-call rota with two people and a 30-minute response time.
a.visionary: We build systems that don't need to wake anyone up.
a.humble: We do, if that's agreed. But let's be upfront about what it costs first.
a.buzzword: Our SRE-driven 24/7 incident ecosystem ensures resilient uptime.

dlv_incident.q: Tell us about a time something went badly wrong in production.

a.concrete: A database migration failed. We rolled back in 20 minutes and wrote a report.
a.visionary: Every failure has made us the vendor we are today.
a.humble: We forgot to check an integration. It was our fault, and we learned a lot.
a.buzzword: We had a learning opportunity that strengthened our resilience and failure culture.

dlv_tech_debt.q: How do you keep technical debt from piling up?

a.concrete: We reserve 20 percent of each sprint for clean-up. It's in the plan.
a.visionary: We build for the next decade, not the next quarter.
a.humble: We can't avoid it entirely. But we'll tell you when we take shortcuts.
a.buzzword: We run a sustainable, architecture-led debt strategy with continuous refactoring.

dlv_inhouse_staff.q: How will you work with our own developers?

a.concrete: In the same team, on the same board. We pair program at least two days a week.
a.visionary: We become one team. Eventually you can't tell who the consultants are.
a.humble: They know your systems better than we do. We have a lot to learn from them.
a.buzzword: We co-create value through cross-functional, hybrid team constellations.

dlv_steering_committee.q: What do you expect from the steering committee?

a.concrete: One meeting a month, quick decisions and one clear owner on your side.
a.visionary: That it holds the course when the wind picks up.
a.humble: That it tells us if we're not delivering what you need. Simple as that.
a.buzzword: Strategic anchoring and governance across the stakeholder landscape.

dlv_sprint_length.q: How long are your sprints, and why?

a.concrete: Two weeks. Short enough to change course, long enough to finish something.
a.visionary: We don't measure in sprints, but in how far we've come.
a.humble: Usually two weeks, but we're happy to match your rhythm.
a.buzzword: We run adaptive iteration cycles calibrated for optimal velocity.

dlv_demo.q: When do we get to see something that actually works?

a.concrete: In two weeks. We'll show you login and the first screen in the test environment.
a.visionary: Soon. And you'll see more than a system – you'll see a direction.
a.humble: Sooner than you'd think, but it'll be rough. That's the point.
a.buzzword: We deliver incremental, demonstrable value from day one.

dlv_bad_news.q: How do you break bad news to us?

a.concrete: The same day, by phone, with a plan for what we do next.
a.visionary: We don't see bad news. We see crossroads.
a.humble: Plainly and early. Better an awkward talk than a surprise.
a.buzzword: Through transparent, trust-based expectation management.

dlv_definition_of_done.q: When is something actually done, in your book?

a.concrete: When it's tested, reviewed, documented and in production.
a.visionary: Never quite. Good systems keep growing.
a.humble: When you say it's done, not when we think it is.
a.buzzword: When it meets our holistic definition of done across the value stream.

dlv_requirements_spec.q: Our requirements spec is 400 pages long. Have you read it?

a.concrete: Yes. We've flagged 38 requirements with questions and brought the list today.
a.visionary: We've read between the lines – and seen what you're really dreaming of.
a.humble: Most of it. Some parts we don't fully understand yet, so we'd like to ask.
a.buzzword: We've done a holistic requirements analysis and mapped it to the target state.

dlv_productivity.q: How do you measure the team's productivity?

a.concrete: Lead time from idea to production, and how many changes we ship a week.
a.visionary: Not in hours, but in how much better your working day becomes.
a.humble: It's harder than it sounds. We'll show you the numbers and what they don't tell you.
a.buzzword: With DORA metrics, velocity tracking and flow-based throughput analysis.

dlv_scope_creep.q: What happens when we ask for just one more little thing?

a.concrete: We estimate it, and you choose what comes out to make room.
a.visionary: We take it as a sign you're seeing even bigger possibilities.
a.humble: We say yes when we can, but we'll also tell you when it isn't that little.
a.buzzword: Our agile change management absorbs scope dynamics seamlessly.

dlv_test_environment.q: We don't have a test environment. Is that a problem?

a.concrete: We'll set one up in the first week. It's about three days' work.
a.visionary: Not a problem – a blank canvas.
a.humble: A bit, yes. But it's common, and we're glad to help get one in place.
a.buzzword: We provision scalable, containerised environments on demand via infrastructure as code.

dlv_release_frequency.q: How often will you release new versions?

a.concrete: Several times a week, in small chunks, always during office hours.
a.visionary: All the time. The system never stands still.
a.humble: As often as you're comfortable with. We'll start carefully.
a.buzzword: We have a fully automated CI/CD value stream with continuous delivery.

dlv_contact.q: How do we reach you if we have a question?

a.concrete: A shared chat channel, answers within two hours on workdays, and one named contact.
a.visionary: Our door is always open. We become part of the house.
a.humble: Any time. No question is too small, and we appreciate them.
a.buzzword: Through an omnichannel communication platform with seamless stakeholder touchpoints.

dlv_vendor_delay.q: What do you do if another vendor holds you up?

a.concrete: We log it as a risk, build a temporary stand-in and keep working.
a.visionary: We don't see others as obstacles, but as fellow travellers on the same journey.
a.humble: We tell you, without pointing fingers. We've been the late one ourselves.
a.buzzword: We decouple dependencies through an API-first, loosely coupled architecture.

dlv_retrospective.q: How do you get better as the project goes on?

a.concrete: A retro every other week, with at most three actions we actually follow up.
a.visionary: We're never done learning. That's the whole point.
a.humble: We ask you regularly what we could do better, and we take it on board.
a.buzzword: Through a continuous improvement culture with built-in feedback loops.

dlv_product_owner.q: We don't have a product owner. Do we need one?

a.concrete: Yes. About half a position, with authority to prioritise. We can help write the role.
a.visionary: You need someone to carry the vision. We'll help you find that person.
a.humble: It helps a lot. We can't make those decisions for you, and we shouldn't.
a.buzzword: We offer product ownership as a service with full business alignment.

dlv_summer_holiday.q: What happens to progress over the summer holidays?

a.concrete: Two people stay on in July, and we freeze all launches from 1 July to 10 August.
a.visionary: Summer is when the best ideas ripen.
a.humble: Things will slow down a bit. We won't pretend otherwise.
a.buzzword: We ensure delivery continuity through a seasonally adjusted capacity model.

dlv_budget_tracking.q: How do we keep track of whether the budget holds?

a.concrete: You get hours and a forecast every month, plus an alert when 80 percent is used.
a.visionary: Think of the budget as an investment in your future, not a cost.
a.humble: We'll warn you well in advance if it looks like overrunning. No surprises.
a.buzzword: Through real-time financial governance and portfolio-level cost insight.

dlv_user_training.q: Who's going to train our staff on the new system?

a.concrete: We'll make a short video series and run two training sessions per department.
a.visionary: We'll build a system so intuitive that training becomes unnecessary.
a.humble: Happy to, together with some of your own people. They know their colleagues best.
a.buzzword: We offer a holistic change management package with digital adoption and super-user networks.

dlv_prototype.q: Could you build a prototype before we decide?

a.concrete: Yes. A clickable prototype in ten days, tested with five of your users.
a.visionary: We can show you the future before it exists.
a.humble: Gladly. That way we'll also find out if we actually work well together.
a.buzzword: We run a rapid design sprint to validate hypotheses and de-risk the solution space.

dlv_monitoring.q: How do you spot errors before the users do?

a.concrete: Alerts on error rate and response time that go straight to the on-call phone.
a.visionary: The goal is a system that tells us how it's feeling.
a.humble: Not always. But when users find something first, we want to hear right away.
a.buzzword: With full-stack observability and predictive anomaly detection.

dlv_tech_decisions.q: Who makes the technical decisions – you or us?

a.concrete: We propose, you approve. Every major choice goes into a decision log.
a.visionary: We make them together, with our eyes on where you'll be in ten years.
a.humble: Ultimately you. You're the ones who have to live with them.
a.buzzword: Through a federated architecture board with clear decision rights and governance.

dlv_rollback.q: Can we roll back if the new version doesn't work?

a.concrete: Yes, with one click. We rehearse rollbacks before every major launch.
a.visionary: We only look forward. But we always have a way home.
a.humble: Yes. And we won't be too proud to do it if we need to.
a.buzzword: We have robust blue-green deployments with automated failover.

dlv_pair_programming.q: We hear you sit two to a computer. Are we paying double?

a.concrete: No. We pair on the hardest parts, about 30 percent of the time, and get fewer bugs.
a.visionary: You're paying for two minds thinking as one.
a.humble: Fair question. We only do it where we think it pays off for you.
a.buzzword: Pairing delivers synergistic knowledge sharing and quality by design.

dlv_green_status.q: With our last vendor, everything was green until it suddenly wasn't. And you?

a.concrete: We report actual deliveries against plan, not gut feeling. You'll see the numbers yourselves.
a.visionary: With us, it's not about colours. It's about direction.
a.humble: We've been too optimistic at times too. So we'd rather call amber too early.
a.buzzword: We have a data-driven, multidimensional status framework with predictive insight.

ppl_seniority_mix.q: What's the mix of seniors and juniors on the team?

a.concrete: Three seniors and two juniors, and each junior has a named senior to pair with.
a.visionary: We blend experience and curiosity into something bigger than the sum.
a.humble: We'd suggest a mix, but we'd rather hear what you need most.
a.buzzword: We run a balanced competence pyramid with scalable seniority.

ppl_resigns.q: What if the consultant resigns in the middle of the project?

a.concrete: Three months' notice, and a replacement is in place before their last day.
a.visionary: Then we'll have built something that survives people moving on.
a.humble: It can happen. We promise to tell you right away, not hide it.
a.buzzword: Our robust transition model ensures a seamless value flow.

ppl_sick_leave.q: What if a consultant goes on long-term sick leave?

a.concrete: We bring in someone new within two weeks, at no extra cost to you.
a.visionary: A strong team carries each other, even when someone drops out.
a.humble: First we look after the person who's ill. Then we find a fix with you.
a.buzzword: We have capacity buffers built into our entire resource ecosystem.

ppl_turnover.q: How high is your staff turnover?

a.concrete: Six per cent last year. Average tenure is five years.
a.visionary: People don't leave us. They become ambassadors.
a.humble: Higher than we'd like last year. We've made changes, and we're tracking it.
a.buzzword: We have sustainable talent retention with positive employer-brand leverage.

ppl_recruiting.q: How do you find good people?

a.concrete: Three interviews, a practical assignment and reference checks for everyone.
a.visionary: We don't look for people. We attract the ones who want to change things.
a.humble: We take our time, and we still get it wrong now and then.
a.buzzword: Through a data-driven talent acquisition funnel with culture-fit scoring.

ppl_onboarding.q: How long before a new consultant is actually useful?

a.concrete: Week one is planned day by day. After two weeks they ship to production.
a.visionary: From day one they bring fresh eyes – that's worth something on its own.
a.humble: Much depends on how we're welcomed. We'll need a bit of help from you.
a.buzzword: We run a streamlined onboarding journey with rapid time-to-value.

ppl_courses.q: How much do you invest in courses and professional development?

a.concrete: Each consultant gets ten learning days and a 30,000-kroner course budget a year.
a.visionary: We invest in our people as if the future depends on it. It does.
a.humble: We do a fair bit, but honestly we learn most from projects like yours.
a.buzzword: We have a continuous learning ecosystem focused on upskilling and reskilling.

a.concrete: Yes. The list of certifications and expiry dates is attached to the bid.
a.visionary: Paperwork is nice, but what we really do is build what comes next.
a.humble: Some are. We won't pretend a course certificate makes anyone an expert.
a.buzzword: We're fully certified across the entire cloud-native value chain.

ppl_diversity.q: How do you work on diversity and inclusion?

a.concrete: We track gender balance in every hiring round and publish the numbers yearly.
a.visionary: We want our team to look like the society it builds solutions for.
a.humble: We're not there yet. We have a lot to learn and welcome your input.
a.buzzword: Diversity is a strategic driver in our inclusive innovation culture.

ppl_office_days.q: How many days a week will you be at our office?

a.concrete: Three fixed days with you – Tuesday to Thursday – and the rest as needed.
a.visionary: We'll be wherever value is created. The office is just the address.
a.humble: As many as you'd like. You know what works best here.
a.buzzword: We run a flexible hybrid-first model with on-demand co-location.

ppl_hybrid.q: How do you collaborate when half the team is working from home?

a.concrete: Fixed stand-up at 9, everything written in one channel, cameras on in workshops.
a.visionary: Distance matters little when everyone sees the same goal.
a.humble: It isn't always easy. We try things out and adjust as we go.
a.buzzword: Through asynchronous collaboration surfaces in a distributed digital workspace.

ppl_overtime.q: What happens when the project needs overtime?

a.concrete: Overtime is agreed in advance, billed per contract and logged weekly.
a.visionary: When something truly matters, we stand together – even late at night.
a.humble: We can stretch for a while, but we'll tell you if it becomes a habit.
a.buzzword: We have elastic capacity that scales dynamically with delivery demand.

ppl_work_life.q: How do you make sure people don't work themselves into the ground?

a.concrete: We review timesheets weekly and step in above 45 hours.
a.visionary: Rested people build better things. That's the whole philosophy.
a.humble: We're not perfect at this. But we ask, and we take the answers seriously.
a.buzzword: We have a holistic well-being framework for sustainable performance.

ppl_conflict.q: How do you handle conflicts within the team?

a.concrete: A talk between those involved, then the team lead, then us within a week.
a.visionary: Friction is where the best ideas are born.
a.humble: We deal with it early and openly – and own up if we're part of the problem.
a.buzzword: Through psychologically safe dialogue arenas and constructive conflict capability.

ppl_bad_fit.q: What do you do if a consultant doesn't fit in here?

a.concrete: Tell us, and you'll have a new candidate to interview within ten days.
a.visionary: Then we find the person who fits – and lifts the whole team.
a.humble: It's a shame, but it happens. We won't take it personally, and we'll fix it.
a.buzzword: We re-match the resource through our cultural alignment process.

ppl_team_lead.q: Who actually leads the team day to day?

a.concrete: Our team lead, with twelve years' experience. She reports to you every Friday.
a.visionary: Leadership is something the whole team takes on. But yes, we have a captain.
a.humble: We should agree on that together. Maybe you have someone who should lead?
a.buzzword: We use a servant leadership model with distributed decision authority.

ppl_domain.q: How will your consultants learn our line of business?

a.concrete: Two days with your experts, a glossary and a fixed Q&A slot every week.
a.visionary: We want to understand you so well we see opportunities you haven't spotted yet.
a.humble: By listening a lot and asking silly questions. You're the experts here.
a.buzzword: Through domain-driven insight capture and cross-functional business understanding.

ppl_norwegian.q: Do all your consultants speak Norwegian?

a.concrete: Four out of five do. The fifth is at B2 level and takes lessons with us.
a.visionary: We speak your users' language. That's what counts.
a.humble: Not all of them. If that matters to you, we'd rather say so up front.
a.buzzword: We're a language-agnostic team with a global mindset and local anchoring.

ppl_clearance.q: Do you have people with security clearance?

a.concrete: Three are cleared to SECRET, and two more applications are in progress.
a.visionary: Trust is the foundation of all we build – including what you can't talk about.
a.humble: A few do. The process takes time, so we should start it early together.
a.buzzword: We have a security-cleared capacity pool with a zero-trust mindset.

a.concrete: We have three, and we measure them in our staff survey twice a year.
a.visionary: We believe in technology that makes the world a bit better, one project at a time.
a.humble: They're on the wall. But you'd probably do better asking our clients.
a.buzzword: We live a values-based, purpose-driven culture with authentic DNA.

ppl_culture_word.q: How would you describe your culture in one word?

a.concrete: “Thorough.” We do what we say, and we write it down.
a.visionary: “Bold.” We dare to think bigger than the brief.
a.humble: It's hard to say about yourself. “Curious,” maybe?
a.buzzword: “Synergistic.” Or “agile.” Possibly “holistic.”

ppl_fagmiljo.q: What kind of professional community do your consultants lean on?

a.concrete: Ten practice groups meeting monthly, and an internal channel that answers within the hour.
a.visionary: A community of people who want to move the whole industry forward.
a.humble: A good one, we think. But judge it by what the team delivers.
a.buzzword: A cross-functional community of practice with strong knowledge synergy.

ppl_knowledge_sharing.q: How do you share lessons across projects?

a.concrete: Lunch talks every Thursday and a shared, searchable lessons-learned base.
a.visionary: What one of us learns, we all learn. That's how we keep pace with the future.
a.humble: We could be better at it, but we ask each other a lot – no question is stupid.
a.buzzword: Through knowledge management that enables learning across silos.

ppl_friday_drinks.q: Will your consultants join our Friday drinks?

a.concrete: Happily, every other Friday. We'll buy our own round, of course.
a.visionary: That table is where the truly great ideas are born.
a.humble: If we're invited, we'd love to. We don't want to intrude.
a.buzzword: We see informal arenas as a key driver of relational value creation.

ppl_cabin_trip.q: Will the consultants be coming on our staff cabin trip too?

a.concrete: If you'd like. Friday counts as a workshop day, and Saturday isn't billable.
a.visionary: It's up in the mountains that you see how far you can go together.
a.humble: That's your call. We'd understand if it's just for your own staff.
a.buzzword: An offsite is a unique opportunity for team alignment and trust building.

ppl_motivation.q: How do you keep your consultants motivated over time?

a.concrete: A one-to-one every quarter and the option to switch projects after two years.
a.visionary: We give them something to believe in. The rest follows.
a.humble: We ask them regularly – and listen, even when it's not what we hoped to hear.
a.buzzword: Through intrinsic motivation design and meaningful engagement architecture.

ppl_burnout.q: What do you do if a consultant is heading for burnout?

a.concrete: Their manager talks to them that week, we lighten the load and follow up.
a.visionary: We build a working life where people flourish, not burn out.
a.humble: We put the person first, even if it costs us. And we'll let you know.
a.buzzword: We have proactive resilience monitoring embedded in our people strategy.

ppl_mentoring.q: Do your juniors have someone to ask when they get stuck?

a.concrete: Yes, everyone has a mentor, with an hour a week booked in the calendar.
a.visionary: We lift the next generation – the people who will one day lift us.
a.humble: Yes, and we tell them it's perfectly fine not to know everything.
a.buzzword: We run a structured mentoring scheme with peer-to-peer learning tracks.

ppl_junior_billing.q: Why should we pay for your juniors to learn on the job?

a.concrete: You shouldn't. The first 100 hours are free, and their rate is lower.
a.visionary: Because you're getting tomorrow's seniors – from day one.
a.humble: That's a fair question. We can set up an arrangement you're comfortable with.
a.buzzword: Juniors deliver a cost-efficient capacity mix with a high learning ROI.

ppl_senior_hands_on.q: Do your seniors still write code, or just slides?

a.concrete: Seniors spend at least 70 per cent of their time coding. It's in the contract.
a.visionary: They write code – and draw the map of where we go next.
a.humble: Admittedly, some have made a few too many slides. We'll pick the coders.
a.buzzword: Our seniors are T-shaped hands-on architects with strategic oversight.

ppl_bench.q: What do your consultants do between assignments?

a.concrete: Internal projects, courses and certifications. It lasts three weeks on average.
a.visionary: They explore what's next. That's where innovation begins.
a.humble: Honestly? They wait, a bit impatiently, for a project like yours.
a.buzzword: They're in a strategic competence-acceleration phase.

ppl_parental_leave.q: What if the consultant goes on parental leave?

a.concrete: We usually know early, so we plan four months' overlap with the replacement.
a.visionary: We're proud to be a place where people can have a life. It makes us stronger.
a.humble: Then we say congratulations – and find an arrangement that works for everyone.
a.buzzword: We use life-phase-adapted resource planning with built-in flexibility.

ppl_underperform.q: How do you deal with a consultant who isn't delivering?

a.concrete: We set concrete goals for four weeks. If they're not met, we swap the person.
a.visionary: We help people find the place where they truly shine.
a.humble: First we want to understand why. Often it's something we should have caught sooner.
a.buzzword: Through a solution-oriented performance dialogue with clear KPIs.

ppl_feedback.q: How can we give feedback on the consultants?

a.concrete: A short form every quarter, and a meeting with us if anything's urgent.
a.visionary: Feedback is the fuel that makes us better with every delivery.
a.humble: Any time, and ideally straight to us. We can take it.
a.buzzword: Through a continuous feedback loop embedded in our customer insight flow.

ppl_one_team.q: Will the consultants join our team, or keep to themselves?

a.concrete: They sit with you, follow your routines and use your tools.
a.visionary: After a month, nobody will be able to tell consultant from employee.
a.humble: We'd like to be part of the team, but you set the terms.
a.buzzword: We operate as a seamlessly integrated one-team with shared ownership.

ppl_train_staff.q: Will you train our own staff along the way?

a.concrete: Yes. One of your people joins every task, and we run two courses every six months.
a.visionary: Our goal is that one day you won't need us.
a.humble: Gladly. We'll probably learn as much from them as they do from us.
a.buzzword: We have a capability-uplifting enablement model for knowledge transfer.

ppl_hire_away.q: What if we'd like to hire your consultant?

a.concrete: It's in the contract: no earlier than twelve months, for an agreed fee.
a.visionary: Then we've done our job. We grow people others want.
a.humble: We'd take that as a compliment. But let's talk about it first.
a.buzzword: We're open to flexible talent mobility models within the partnership.

a.concrete: No. Average age is 38, and the eldest has worked in IT since 1989.
a.visionary: We're young at heart – and that's where innovation lives.
a.humble: We look young on our website. In reality we're more of a mix.
a.buzzword: We have a generationally diverse team with cross-generational synergy.

ppl_scale_up.q: How quickly can you scale up if we need more people?

a.concrete: Two more in two weeks and five more within six. We already have names.
a.visionary: We grow in step with your ambitions – however big they get.
a.humble: A little, quickly. A lot takes time, and we won't send you the wrong people.
a.buzzword: We offer on-demand scalability in an elastic delivery ecosystem.

ppl_dress_code.q: Will the consultants turn up in suits or hoodies?

a.concrete: We follow your dress code. Suits for board meetings, otherwise like everyone else.
a.visionary: We dress for the future. Apparently it wears a hoodie.
a.humble: You tell us. We'd rather not stand out.
a.buzzword: We have a contextual, stakeholder-adapted dress-code strategy.

ppl_working_hours.q: When during the day can we expect to reach the consultants?

a.concrete: Core hours are 9 to 3, and everyone replies within an hour during that time.
a.visionary: We're there when it matters. Good ideas don't watch the clock.
a.humble: Normal working hours. We have families too, but we'll show up if things catch fire.
a.buzzword: We ensure availability through a flexible, asynchronous response model.

ppl_account_follow_up.q: Who on your side follows up the consultants along the way?

a.concrete: A dedicated account manager, with a status meeting at your office every six weeks.
a.visionary: The whole company stands behind them. That's what you're really buying.
a.humble: One of the partners. And if something isn't working, we want you to call us.
a.buzzword: We have a holistic stakeholder management structure with close governance.

ppl_tenure.q: How long have the proposed consultants been with you?

a.concrete: Between two and eleven years. It's all in the CV appendix.
a.visionary: Long enough to know us – short enough to still be hungry.
a.humble: One of them started last year. We'd rather just say so.
a.buzzword: We have a balanced tenure profile with strong organisational anchoring.

ppl_soft_skills.q: Can your developers talk to normal people?

a.concrete: Yes. All have run user tests, and two have taught courses for caseworkers.
a.visionary: They build bridges between technology and people. That's the whole point.
a.humble: Most can. And the quieter ones are good listeners.
a.buzzword: Our developers have strong stakeholder communication and empathic design thinking.

ppl_speak_up.q: Will your consultants dare to speak up when we're wrong?

a.concrete: Yes. Risks and disagreements are a fixed item at every status meeting.
a.visionary: We're not here to agree with you. We're here to make you better.
a.humble: We try, respectfully. But we know we're not always right ourselves.
a.buzzword: We have a psychologically safe speak-up culture with radical transparency.

ppl_learning_days.q: Do the consultants take learning days on our dime?

a.concrete: No. We pay for learning days, and they always fall between your sprints.
a.visionary: Every learning day comes back to you as fresh ideas.
a.humble: No, of course not. But we'll give you plenty of notice when someone's away.
a.buzzword: The competence uplift is a value-adding contribution to the partnership.

tec_cloud_provider.q: Which cloud provider do you recommend?

a.concrete: It depends on your requirements. We compare three providers on price, operations and data location.
a.visionary: The cloud isn't a place, it's a way of thinking. We'll pick the one that takes you furthest.
a.humble: We have no favourite to push. Tell us what you need and we'll help you choose.
a.buzzword: We recommend a cloud-agnostic, hybrid multi-cloud strategy with cloud native as a guiding principle.

tec_vendor_lockin.q: How do we avoid getting locked in to a single vendor?

a.concrete: Open formats, standard APIs and an exit plan we actually rehearse once a year.
a.visionary: Freedom is a design choice. We build systems you can always leave – which is why you'll stay.
a.humble: Avoiding it completely is hard. But we can be honest about where the ties are and what they cost.
a.buzzword: With a portable, containerised platform abstraction that decouples the value stream from infrastructure.

tec_open_source.q: What's your view on open source?

a.concrete: We use a lot of it, check licences automatically and pick projects with active maintainers.
a.visionary: Open source is humanity's greatest group effort. We want you to be part of it.
a.humble: We stand on the shoulders of many volunteers, and try to give a little back where we can.
a.buzzword: We embrace an open, community-driven innovation ecosystem with co-creation built in.

tec_microservices.q: Should we split the system into microservices?

a.concrete: Maybe not. With one team of six, a tidy monolith is often faster and cheaper.
a.visionary: Your architecture should mirror the organisation you want to become, not the one you are today.
a.humble: We'd like to understand the problem first. Microservices solve some things and create others.
a.buzzword: We recommend a domain-driven, event-based modular micro-architecture with clear bounded contexts.

tec_architecture_decisions.q: How do you make architecture decisions?

a.concrete: Every decision goes on one page: context, options, choice and consequences.
a.visionary: We draw a north star, and let every decision bring us a little closer.
a.humble: Together with you. And we write down why, so it's easy to admit when we got it wrong.
a.buzzword: Through a federated, evolutionary architecture forum with data-driven decision gates.

tec_data_driven.q: We want to become data-driven. Where do we start?

a.concrete: With three questions management actually wants answered, and the data needed to answer them.
a.visionary: Picture an organisation where every decision is made with its eyes open. That's where we're going.
a.humble: We'd start by hearing which decisions you find hard to make today.
a.buzzword: With a data mesh-based insight ecosystem that democratises data end-to-end.

tec_data_quality.q: Our data is pretty messy. Is that a problem?

a.concrete: We measure first: duplicates, empty fields and bad formats. Then we fix the ten worst sources.
a.visionary: Messy data is just stories waiting to be told properly.
a.humble: Everyone has messy data, us included. What matters is that you know about it, and you do.
a.buzzword: We establish a data governance framework with proactive quality observability and clear data ownership.

a.concrete: We only store what we need, delete on fixed schedules and have a data processing agreement in place.
a.visionary: Privacy is trust, and trust is the only currency that matters online.
a.humble: We're not lawyers, so we involve your data protection officer early and would rather ask once too often.
a.buzzword: With privacy by design as an integral part of a trust-based, compliance-oriented delivery model.

a.concrete: We follow WCAG level AA, test automatically on every build and manually with a screen reader before launch.
a.visionary: A service that isn't for everyone isn't finished. We build for everyone.
a.humble: We still make mistakes here. That's why we test with real users, who often find what we miss.
a.buzzword: Accessibility is an inclusive quality dimension we shift left across the entire value stream.

tec_accessibility_audit.q: The regulator found 47 accessibility violations. What now?

a.concrete: We sort them by severity, fix the critical ones in four weeks and update the accessibility statement.
a.visionary: This isn't a crisis, it's an invitation to become the most accessible service in the country.
a.humble: It's annoying, but it's good they were found. We'd like to read the report first.
a.buzzword: We mobilise a cross-functional remediation programme with continuous compliance monitoring.

a.concrete: Password manager for everyone, two-factor everywhere and no secrets in code. Checked automatically.
a.visionary: We look forward to the day passwords are museum pieces. That day is closer than you think.
a.humble: A strained one, like everyone's. That's why we trust tools rather than our own memory.
a.buzzword: We follow a passwordless, identity-centric zero trust model with continuous verification.

a.concrete: Yes, an external test before launch and once a year after. Findings are closed within an agreed deadline.
a.visionary: We think like an attacker, so you never have to meet a real one.
a.humble: We test ourselves, but we recommend someone from outside does it too. We're too fond of our own code.
a.buzzword: We offer offensive security as a service, integrated into a holistic threat-led approach.

tec_supply_chain.q: How do you handle vulnerabilities in third-party libraries?

a.concrete: We scan dependencies on every build, keep a bill of materials and patch critical issues within 48 hours.
a.visionary: Software is a food chain. We look after every single link.
a.humble: We use hundreds of packages we didn't write. We can't promise zero, but we keep a close eye.
a.buzzword: With shift-left supply chain security and real-time SBOM-driven risk insight.

tec_logging.q: What do you log, and how long do you keep it?

a.concrete: Events and errors, no personal data. Kept for 90 days, access logs for a year.
a.visionary: Logs are the system's memory. We make sure it remembers what matters.
a.humble: As little as possible, and we should agree that with you. We've logged too much before.
a.buzzword: We have a centralised, structured telemetry strategy with policy-driven lifecycle management.

tec_security_incident.q: What do you do if we get hacked?

a.concrete: We follow an incident plan: isolate, notify within 72 hours, restore and write a report.
a.visionary: Then we stand with you, and come out the other side stronger than before.
a.humble: We call you straight away, even if it's our fault. Especially then.
a.buzzword: We activate a resilient, event-driven response framework with cross-functional crisis synergy.

tec_performance.q: Our solution is slow. What would you do?

a.concrete: Measure first. Usually three slow queries and one oversized image account for most of it.
a.visionary: Speed is a feeling. We want users to feel the service is one step ahead of them.
a.humble: We'd ask where users feel it's slow. It's not always where we'd guess.
a.buzzword: We'd run end-to-end performance optimisation powered by observability-driven insight.

tec_peak_load.q: What happens when everyone logs in on deadline day?

a.concrete: We load test at ten times normal traffic and set up autoscaling. And a queue page.
a.visionary: That's when the service shines. Deadline day becomes the day people say nice things about you.
a.humble: It's the day we dread the most. That's why we rehearse it well in advance.
a.buzzword: An elastic, scalable platform handles peak load seamlessly through automated capacity.

tec_app_vs_web.q: Do we need an app, or is a website enough?

a.concrete: Your users visit twice a year. A good mobile-friendly website will do.
a.visionary: The question isn't app or web. It's where in your users' lives you want to be.
a.humble: We don't know yet. Let's ask some users before spending money on either.
a.buzzword: We recommend a mobile-first, omnichannel customer journey with cross-platform synergy.

tec_offline.q: Our people work in the mountains with no signal. Is that doable?

a.concrete: Yes. The app stores data locally and syncs when you're back online. We've tested it in a tunnel.
a.visionary: Technology should follow people where they are, not just where the masts are.
a.humble: It's harder than it sounds. Could we join you in the field one day to see how you work?
a.buzzword: With an offline-first, event-based sync architecture at the edge of the network.

tec_design_system.q: Why should we spend money on a design system?

a.concrete: Because you have twelve different buttons today. Shared components save time on every screen.
a.visionary: A design system is a shared language. It lets the whole organisation speak with one voice.
a.humble: Maybe you shouldn't yet. It only pays off once several teams are building screens.
a.buzzword: A scalable, token-based design system drives brand consistency and developer synergy across the board.

a.concrete: We pick what your team can run, what's been stable for five years and what's easy to hire for.
a.visionary: We choose the tech you'll be proud of in ten years, not the one that's trendy this year.
a.humble: We have our favourites, but you're the ones who'll live with it. We'd like to hear what you know.
a.buzzword: Through a future-proof, cloud-based tech radar framework with evidence-based assessment.

tec_new_framework.q: Our developers want to use a brand-new framework. Is that wise?

a.concrete: Maybe. Try it in one small module for two weeks and measure whether it's actually faster.
a.visionary: Curiosity is the engine of all innovation. We shouldn't stifle it.
a.humble: We've said yes to new frameworks we later regretted. Happy to share what we learned.
a.buzzword: A modern, component-based framework can significantly accelerate the developer journey.

a.concrete: Versioning, clear error messages, up-to-date docs and examples that actually work.
a.visionary: A good API is an open door. It lets others build things you never imagined.
a.humble: That the people using it find it easy. We ask them rather than assume.
a.buzzword: API-first, contract-driven and consumer-centric, as part of a composable enterprise.

tec_integrations.q: We have over forty integrations. How do we get an overview?

a.concrete: We map them all, with owner, format and what happens when they fail. Takes about three weeks.
a.visionary: Every integration is a relationship. We'll help you see the whole network.
a.humble: Sounds like something you've been wrestling with for a while. Who knows the most about them today?
a.buzzword: With an event-driven integration platform that seamlessly orchestrates data across silos.

tec_migration.q: How do we move data from the old system to the new one?

a.concrete: We run trial migrations weekly, reconcile totals against the source and have a rollback plan.
a.visionary: A migration is a move. It's a chance to bring only what truly matters.
a.humble: Carefully. Migrations almost always take longer than planned, and we'd rather say that now.
a.buzzword: Through a phased, de-risked modernisation journey with automated data lineage.

tec_cloud_cost.q: Our cloud bill has doubled. What do we do?

a.concrete: We tag every resource with an owner, shut down what's idle and set budget alerts.
a.visionary: The cloud should give you freedom, not worry. We'll turn the bill into a tool.
a.humble: It happens to a lot of people. We'd like to look at the bill with you before saying more.
a.buzzword: We introduce FinOps as a cross-functional cost optimisation culture with real-time unit economics.

tec_data_location.q: Does our data have to be stored in Norway?

a.concrete: Not necessarily, but within the EEA. We document where everything is and who has access.
a.visionary: Your data is part of society's memory. It deserves a safe home.
a.humble: That's a legal question we don't want to answer too quickly. Let's take it to your lawyers.
a.buzzword: We ensure sovereign data residency through a regionally anchored, compliance-governed cloud architecture.

tec_devops.q: What does DevOps mean to you, concretely?

a.concrete: The team that writes the code also runs it, with monitoring, on-call duty and ownership of bugs.
a.visionary: That the wall between those who build and those who operate finally comes down.
a.humble: The word means different things to everyone. What does it mean to you? Let's start there.
a.buzzword: A cultural transformation towards cross-functional, automated and continuous flow of value.

tec_backup.q: When did you last test that a backup can actually be restored?

a.concrete: Last month. We restore to a test environment automatically every week and log how long it takes.
a.visionary: A backup is a promise to the future. We keep our promises.
a.humble: Honestly? Too long ago. And last time it didn't go entirely well. We learned from that.
a.buzzword: We have a robust, policy-based data resilience strategy with automated recovery validation.

tec_disaster_recovery.q: What do we do if the whole data centre goes down?

a.concrete: We keep copies in another region, a two-page plan and aim to be back up within four hours.
a.visionary: That's when we find out if we've built something that can withstand the world. And we have.
a.humble: It's scary to think about, but we have to. We suggest we rehearse it together once a year.
a.buzzword: Through a geo-redundant, self-healing architecture with built-in business continuity.

tec_green_it.q: How do you approach sustainable IT?

a.concrete: We turn off test environments at night, pick data centres on renewables and measure usage.
a.visionary: Every line of code leaves a footprint on the planet. We want yours to be a light one.
a.humble: We're no experts, and we probably travel too much. But we try to get the simple things right.
a.buzzword: With a climate-neutral, circular digitalisation strategy and ESG-integrated value creation.

tec_chatbot.q: Can we get a chatbot on our website?

a.concrete: Yes, but we'd first look at the 20 most common questions. Many are solved by a better page.
a.visionary: Picture a service that's always awake, always patient and always kind.
a.humble: We can, but a lot of users find them annoying. We'd like to test it before you decide.
a.buzzword: An AI-powered conversational assistant delivers a hyper-personalised, seamless omnichannel experience.

tec_ai_own_data.q: Can we use AI on our own documents?

a.concrete: Yes. We start with one archive, a hundred test questions and measure how often it's right.
a.visionary: Everything the organisation has ever known, available to everyone in seconds. That's the future.
a.humble: It can work well, but it's sometimes wrong with great confidence. You should know that up front.
a.buzzword: With a RAG-based knowledge platform that unlocks the value in unstructured data.

tec_ai_code.q: Do you use AI to write the code?

a.concrete: Yes, as a tool. All code is read and approved by a human and passes the same tests.
a.visionary: We're in the middle of the biggest shift in the craft since the compiler. We want to lead it.
a.humble: A bit. It's fast, but it gets things wrong. So we read everything it suggests, and we're open about it.
a.buzzword: We have an AI-augmented, agentic development flow that 10x-es productivity.

tec_ai_risk.q: What if the AI solution gives citizens wrong answers?

a.concrete: We log answers, spot-check weekly and always show the source and a way to reach a human.
a.visionary: We build AI with a conscience. Trust isn't a feature, it's a foundation.
a.humble: It will happen. The point is to catch it fast and say so, not to pretend it doesn't.
a.buzzword: With a responsible AI framework built on explainability, guardrails and human-in-the-loop governance.

tec_low_code.q: Couldn't we just use a low-code tool instead?

a.concrete: For simple forms and internal workflows, yes. Beyond a few integrations it gets expensive fast.
a.visionary: Low-code hands power back to those who know the problem. It's a small revolution.
a.humble: Maybe. Then you'd need us less, and we're happy to say so.
a.buzzword: Low-code enables citizen developers and hyperautomation in a composable enterprise.

tec_login.q: How should our users log in?

a.concrete: Through the national login service for citizens, and work accounts for your own staff.
a.visionary: Logging in should be so easy nobody notices. That's the best a login can hope for.
a.humble: Depends on who they are. We'd like to see how they log in today and what they struggle with.
a.buzzword: Through a federated, seamless digital identity journey with adaptive authentication.

tec_national_components.q: Do you use the shared national components, or build your own?

a.concrete: We use them where they exist: login, digital mail and registries. We've integrated with all of them.
a.visionary: Every shared component is a brick in a common digital nation. We build on it, not beside it.
a.humble: We use them. They're not always perfect, but building your own is almost always worse.
a.buzzword: We leverage the national ecosystem to realise joined-up services and cross-sector benefits.

tec_archiving.q: How do you meet the requirements of the archives act?

a.concrete: We clarify archiving duties early with your archivists and export to an approved format automatically.
a.visionary: We're writing history. In a hundred years, someone should be able to read what was decided today.
a.humble: It's a field we respect and don't know everything about. We'd like your archivist involved from day one.
a.buzzword: Through lifecycle-oriented information management with built-in preservation automation.

tec_spreadsheet.q: Half our operations run on one spreadsheet. Is that a problem?

a.concrete: Only if just one person understands it, or it isn't backed up. We'd check both first.
a.visionary: That spreadsheet is a prototype of the system you really need. We should honour it.
a.humble: Not necessarily. It works. We'd be careful touching it before we understand it.
a.buzzword: We can transform it into a scalable, cloud-based process platform with built-in automation.

tec_realtime.q: Management wants everything in real time. What does that involve?

a.concrete: It costs more. Most reports are fine with overnight data. We find the ones that really need to be fresh.
a.visionary: Real time means the organisation sees the world as it is now, not as it was yesterday.
a.humble: We'd ask what they'd do differently with the numbers if they arrived sooner.
a.buzzword: With a streaming, event-driven real-time architecture delivering instant insight.

tec_open_data.q: We're going to publish open data. How do we do it right?

a.concrete: Open licence, machine-readable format, a simple API and a description of every field. No personal data.
a.visionary: Open data is fuel for a thousand services you'll never have to build yourselves.
a.humble: We'd talk to people who'll actually use the data first. Otherwise it's easy to share the wrong thing.
a.buzzword: We establish an open data ecosystem that catalyses cross-sector value creation and innovation.

tec_search.q: Users can't find anything with our search. Can you fix it?

a.concrete: We look at the hundred most common searches with no hits and add synonyms. That often fixes half of it.
a.visionary: Search is about understanding what people mean, not just what they type.
a.humble: We can try. Often the problem is the content, not the search engine, so we'd look at both.
a.buzzword: With semantic, AI-powered search and context-aware, real-time relevance optimisation.

com_fixed_price.q: Can you deliver this at a fixed price?

a.concrete: Yes, for phase one. We'll price the rest after four weeks of real data.
a.visionary: The price is fixed. The possibilities aren't.
a.humble: We can, but then we have to be honest about how uncertain the estimate is.
a.buzzword: We'd recommend a hybrid, value-based pricing model with agile delivery gates.

sec_ministry_press_conference.q: The minister wants something to show off at a press conference in six weeks.

a.concrete: We can do that if we pick one service and finish it for one user group, rather than half-finish it for all.
a.visionary: Then we won't just show a service, but a whole new way for government to meet people.
a.humble: We can try. But better the minister shows something small that works than something big that doesn't.
a.buzzword: We deliver a high-profile, user-centric pilot with rapid time-to-value and clear benefits realisation.

sec_members_board_passwords.q: Our board changes every year, and nobody knows the passwords. Can you help?

a.concrete: Yes. We tie access to roles instead of people, with a simple handover checklist for every AGM.
a.visionary: An association should outlive every board. We build for the next fifty years.
a.humble: It's more common than you'd think. We'd start by finding out who actually holds the keys today.
a.buzzword: We introduce holistic, role-based identity and access management with seamless board transition.

crisisTalk.timeout: You stood there thinking. It was noted.
crisisTalk.question: Question {{n}} of 3

tier.good: That went well. People left feeling somebody is in control.
tier.ok: That went fine. Nobody will remember it in a week.
tier.bad: That went badly. A quote of yours is already doing the rounds.

reactions.love: A few nods. It feels like a turning point.
reactions.hate: The room goes quiet. Not the good kind of quiet.

press.title: Press conference
press.intro: Five journalists, two cameras and a microphone that squeals. You have {{seconds}} seconds per question.

who_knew.q: When did management know about this?

a.candid: We knew on Tuesday. We should have said so on Tuesday.
a.caring: Our first thought was the people affected. That's why we called them before we called you.
a.facts: The alert came at 09:14 on Tuesday. Measures were in place by 11:40. The full timeline is on our website.
a.spin: We have maintained a proactive, holistic focus on this from day one.

a.caring: We take responsibility as a company, and we're looking after the team in the middle of it.
a.facts: A change went out without review. We've checked 214 similar changes, and none had the same flaw.
a.spin: This is a challenge the whole industry needs to tackle together.

a.candid: Yes, if we change nothing. So we're changing things.
a.caring: We'll do everything we can so nobody has to go through this again.
a.facts: We've added three new checks and an external audit every six months.
a.spin: We are now better equipped than ever to meet the challenges of the future.

affected.q: What do you say to the people affected?

a.caring: That we understand they're worried, and they can call us directly. We answer around the clock.
a.facts: It affects 1,400 people. All of them have had a letter, and we've already spoken to 92 per cent.
a.spin: Fortunately, the vast majority haven't noticed anything at all.

a.candid: No. I'm going to fix this, and you can hold me to it.
a.caring: Right now the most important thing is to be here for the team and our clients.
a.facts: The board has considered it and given me three concrete targets by New Year.
a.spin: I have never been more motivated to take the company into its next phase.

clues.candid: The journalists have talked to sources. They know more than you think.
clues.caring: The papers are mostly writing about the people affected.
clues.facts: It's the trade press, and they've brought spreadsheets.
clues.spin: It's late in the news day. They just need a quote for the web story.

townhall.title: All-hands
townhall.intro: The whole firm in the canteen. Someone brought popcorn. You have {{seconds}} seconds per question.

why_now.q: Why are we only hearing about this now?

a.candid: Because we were too slow. That's on me.
a.caring: Because we wanted to protect the people involved. But I know it's been a heavy week for you.
a.facts: We found out nine days ago. The lawyers asked us to wait until the facts were checked.
a.spin: We have communicated in line with our values of openness throughout.

safe.q: Is it safe to speak up here?

a.candid: Not safe enough, it seems. We have to fix that.
a.caring: It should be. And you can always come to me, after hours too.
a.facts: From next month we'll have an external whistleblowing channel. Every case gets an answer within five days.
a.spin: There's a policy for that on the intranet.

a.candid: Maybe. I'll tell you as soon as I know.
a.caring: I know a lot of you are worried. Nobody will get a nasty surprise in the post.
a.facts: Profit drops by about three per cent. The bonus model is unchanged.
a.spin: Let's stay focused on what matters here.

trust.q: Why should we trust management now?

a.candid: Don't take our word for it. Watch what we do.
a.caring: Because we're in this together, and I'll be standing here until it's sorted.
a.facts: We'll publish progress every Friday, with numbers. You can check for yourselves.

a.candid: We clean it up, and it'll be uncomfortable for a while.
a.caring: Now we look after each other. There's cake in the canteen, and my door is open.
a.facts: Three actions. I'll email them after this meeting, with owners and deadlines.

clues.candid: People are angry, and they've noticed when they were talked around.
clues.caring: People are mostly tired and scared. Many haven't slept well.
clues.facts: The developers have already started a Slack thread full of questions and numbers.
clues.spin: Half the firm is at client sites, watching the stream on mute.

client.title: Crisis meeting with the client
client.intro: The client's leadership team sits in a row. Nobody has taken their coat off. You have {{seconds}} seconds per question.

a.candid: We made a mistake. Full stop.
a.caring: First: we understand this has hit you and your users hard.
a.facts: Here's the timeline minute by minute, and here's the root cause.
a.spin: It's a complex matter with lots of learning points for all parties.

fix.q: What are you doing to put it right?

a.candid: Our best person is on it, and it costs you nothing.
a.caring: We're here for as long as it takes. You'll have my mobile number.
a.facts: Four actions with deadlines, and a status report every Friday.
a.spin: We propose a pre-study to map the need.

money.q: Why should we pay for this?

a.candid: You shouldn't. This one's on us.
a.caring: We don't want this to spoil a good partnership. Let's find a solution together.
a.facts: We'll credit 38 hours. That's what the fault cost you.
a.spin: The contract is fairly clear on that point.

again.q: How do we know it won't happen again?

a.candid: You don't. But you'll see everything we do to prevent it.
a.caring: Because we care about what you're building, and we're watching extra closely now.
a.facts: Review on everything, automated tests right here, and you get access to the logs.

trust.q: Why should we keep working with you?

a.candid: Because we tell you when something goes wrong. Like now.
a.caring: Because we know your people, and we want them to succeed.
a.facts: We've delivered on time in 94 per cent of sprints.

clues.candid: The client has been around a long time and hates excuses.
clues.caring: Their contact person has been told off by their own management over this.
clues.facts: The client brought their head of procurement and an engineer with a notepad.
clues.spin: The client's management just needs a nice line to pass on to the board.

learned.candid: They wanted straight honesty. Worth remembering.
learned.caring: They needed to feel seen and looked after. Worth remembering.
learned.facts: They wanted facts, numbers and a plan. Worth remembering.
learned.spin: They just wanted a nice turn of phrase. No judgement.

invaders.title: Meeting Invaders
invaders.intro: Your calendar is under attack. Decline the meetings before they reach your desk.
invaders.controls: Arrow keys or A/D to move, space to decline. Esc to give up.

endings.calendarFull: Your calendar is full. You're in meetings until 2036.
endings.outOfCoffee: Out of coffee. You're accepting everything now.

standup.title: Stand-up Bingo
standup.intro: Today's stand-up has started. Mark the phrases as people say them and get four in a row. Don't mark anything nobody's said, because the team lead is watching.

endings.bingo: BINGO! You said it out loud. The team lead pretends nothing happened.
endings.over: The stand-up ran for 45 minutes. No bingo.
endings.caught: The team lead asks if you're paying attention. You aren't.
